subtype: Approach: task decomposition into a packing and route list [Action]
passage: A week before the holidays, Sarita sat down with her mother Mehak and a blank sheet. "We're going to Nani's. What has to happen?" She wrote in a column: book tickets, pack clothes, food for the train, tell Nani the arrival time. Each item got a small box. Mummy booked the tickets that evening, and Sarita ticked her first box with a red pen. On Wednesday they packed together, on Thursday they made theplas, and the last box, call Nani, was ticked on Friday. On Saturday the train was on time, and there was nothing left to remember at the last minute.

qa.q: What items were on Sarita's list?
qa.a: The list had book tickets, pack clothes, food for the train and tell Nani the arrival time.

qa.q: What was Sarita feeling as she ticked the last box?
qa.a: Satisfied and calm, since everything had been handled before the day.

qa.q: What other step could Sarita add to the list, and why?
qa.a: She could check the tickets and ID the day before, so a small mistake is found while there is still time.

qa.q: How might Mehak see Sarita's list?
qa.a: Mehak may find it helpful and be proud, since Sarita shares the planning and the ticking.

grounding: A girl breaks a visit to her grandparents into tasks, and ticks them off with her mother the week before.

subtype: Approach: task decomposition into a packing and route list [Action]
passage:
"Maa, I've made the list for Dida and Dadu's."
"Rajni, it's a week away!" Bidisha laughed. "Let me see."
"One: tickets. Two: pack clothes. Three: food for the train. Four: a gift for Dida."
"Tickets are done. Baba booked them yesterday."
"Tick!" Rajni drew a fat tick. "Clothes I'll pack on Thursday. Two frocks, the shawl Dida likes, and my slippers."
"And the train food?"
"Luchi and aloo dum, packed the night before. Water bottles. Paper plates."
"Plates? Your Baba forgets plates every single time."
"That's why I wrote it big." Rajni underlined it twice. "Five: ask Mitali-mashi to feed Tommy."
"The dog! I forgot about the dog."
"Tick, when she says yes."

qa.q: What will Rajni pack on Thursday?
qa.a: Two frocks, the shawl Dida likes, and her slippers.

qa.q: How does Rajni seem to feel while working through the list?
qa.a: She seems proud and eager, drawing a fat tick and underlining the plates twice. 😊

qa.q: What else could make Rajni's list even more useful?
qa.a: Writing a day beside each task, so the jobs are spread through the week instead of piling up the night before.

qa.q: How does Bidisha experience the list?
qa.a: Bidisha is amused and impressed, and relieved when Rajni remembers the dog she had forgotten.

grounding: A girl breaks a visit to her grandparents into tasks and ticks them off with her mother a week ahead.

subtype: Approach: task decomposition into a packing and route list [Action]
passage: Last Diwali, when we went to see Nani and Nana in Nagpur, Mummy let me, Seema, be the list-maker. A week before, I sat at the dining table with a pad and broke the trip into jobs: tickets, clothes for four days, food for the twelve-hour train, a present for Nana, and someone to water our plants. Every evening Mummy and I went down the list together. Some jobs took one minute; my little sister Indu packed her own socks. Some took three evenings, like finding Nana's favourite tea. On the day we left, the only thing not ticked was "relax". On the train, while other families ran to buy food at stations, we opened our steel tiffins and ate slowly. I felt very grown-up.

qa.q: How long was the train journey?
How did Seema feel on the train?
qa.a: Seema felt proud and grown-up, eating calmly while other families rushed for food.

qa.q: Which other approach could work for a trip like this, and why?
qa.a: Starting from an old checklist of past trips would save time, but breaking this trip into its own jobs fitted what this visit needed.

qa.q: What was it like for Indu to be part of the plan?
qa.a: Indu got a small job of her own, packing her own socks, so she was included too.

grounding: Looking back, a child describes breaking a family visit into tasks and checking them off with Mummy the week before.
